sections.title: Bar Elements Description (Mini-Bar)
sections.content:
The Mini-Bar is a floating bar designed to take up minimal screen space while providing maximum control. Description of elements from left to right:

  • ● (Status Dot): Indicates the validity of the selected environment.
    • Green: Environment is OK and exists on disk.
    • Red: Environment does not exist or its path is invalid.
  • INFO Text / Group List: Displays the name of the current project and Venv (in Single mode), or the list of groups (in Multi mode).

  • (VS Code): Opens the current project directly in VS Code with the properly linked environment and user profile.
  • ▶ Play: Launches the assigned script or the entire group.
  • ■ Stop: Immediately terminates the running script or the entire group.
  • ⚙ (Gear): Opens/Closes the Quick Settings panel.
  • 🖥 (Monitor): Opens the full Master Manager window for advanced management.
  • 📌 (Pin): Toggles 'Always on Top' mode. When active, the bar stays above other windows.
  • (Mode Switch): Toggles between Single mode (individual project) and Multi mode (batch launching).
  • ✕ (Close): Completely exits the entire VenvHub Pro application.

sections.title: Quick Settings (Slide-out Panel)
sections.content:
Clicking the gear icon (⚙) slides out a panel that allows you to quickly adjust parameters without having to open the full Manager.

What can you configure here?

  1. Project, Venv, and VS Code Profile: Quickly switch projects and their environments, including isolated editor profiles.
  2. Startup Script: Displays which file will be executed. This path is configured in the main Manager, not here.
  3. Language: Allows instant changes to the application language. (Note: Theme/skin changes are performed in the main Manager window).
  4. Quick Install (Pip/UV): Enter a package name (e.g. requests) and click Install. The package will be installed using your configured default installer.

sections.title: Environment Switching and Synchronization (Master Override)
sections.content:
In older versions of VenvHub, the Quick Settings panel only served for temporary in-memory environment changes. In the current version (Pro), this is no longer the case!

If you change the Venv or VS Code profile in the Quick Settings panel, the system executes a Master Override:

  • The environment is immediately saved to the configuration file and becomes the permanent default for the given project.
  • The system automatically synchronizes VS Code in the background (updates the settings.json file) so the editor uses this new Venv upon launch.
  • The VenvHub Linker also runs automatically in the background, updating paths and tasks in VS Code for all your local packages.

sections.title: Execution Modes
sections.content:
In the '3. Actions' section, you can choose how the Play ▶ button behaves:

  • Open Terminal: Does not execute the script, but only opens a command prompt (CMD) activated in the selected environment. Suitable if you want to enter commands manually.
  • Run in Terminal (Default): Opens a new window, activates the venv, and automatically runs your script. You see all output (prints) and errors.
  • Run in Background (Silent): The script runs without any visible window (invisibly). Ideal for production applications, GUI programs, or background processes.
Note on Silent mode: Since no window is visible, you must terminate the script either using the Stop ■ button on the bar or via Task Manager.

sections.title: Multi-run Mode on Mini-Bar
sections.content:
When you click the mode switch button (), the Mini-Bar switches to batch launch mode. The interface adjusts:

  • Instead of project text, a dropdown list appears with all your groups created in the Manager.
  • The Quick Settings button (⚙) and (VS Code) icon are automatically hidden, as single-project settings do not apply in this mode.
  • The Play ▶ and Stop ■ buttons now control the entire selected group at once.
Advantage: In this mode, you do not need to open the main window. Simply select a group from the bar and launch or stop all servers and processes belonging to it with a single click.
